changes.oldRationale: Smart Locators analyze potentially hundreds of attributes per element, weight them, and adapt across runs — so if some attributes change, the element can still be found using others. This is what keeps tests from breaking on every small UI tweak.
changes.newRationale: Weighted attributes support resilient element identification. Changing attributes may still leave useful matching evidence; this does not guarantee every changed UI succeeds or that outcome assertions are unnecessary.

changes.oldQuestion: Why is a Wait For step generally preferred over a fixed-time delay before an asynchronous element appears?
changes.newQuestion: Why is a Wait For step generally preferred over a fixed-time delay before an asynchronous element appears?
oldKey: Wait For pauses exactly until the condition is true, avoiding both flaky too-short waits and wasteful too-long waits.
newKey: It checks the readiness condition until detected or timeout, reducing dependence on a guessed fixed delay.
changes.oldRationale: A Wait For step pauses until a specific condition (e.g. element visible) becomes true, so the test waits exactly as long as needed — avoiding the flakiness of a too-short fixed delay and the wasted time of a too-long one.
changes.newRationale: Condition-based waits synchronize with detected readiness up to the configured timeout. They do not guarantee exact timing, faster execution in every case or elimination of all failures; Sleep remains supported.

changes.oldQuestion: How is the Testim REST API key used to authenticate a standard request?
changes.newQuestion: How is the Testim REST API key used to authenticate a standard request?
oldKey: In the Authorization header as a Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer PAK-[your-api-key].
newKey: In Authorization: Bearer followed by the copied PAK-prefixed API key.

changes.newRationale: The Authorization Bearer value is the copied API key. Encrypted-credential access has an additional authorized-user header, not replacement authentication.

changes.oldQuestion: How can a single login group be reused across tests that each need different credentials?
changes.newQuestion: How can a shared login group be reused with different credentials?
oldKey: By adding JavaScript parameters for username and password in the group's properties panel.
newKey: Define group username/password parameters and bind the credential entry steps to them.
changes.oldRationale: Adding JavaScript parameters for username and password in the group properties panel makes the group generic — each use of the group can then supply different credentials without duplicating steps.
changes.newRationale: Parameters must actually be referenced by the group’s entry steps; defining unused parameters does not replace hardcoded values.

changes.oldQuestion: Why is incognito mode particularly useful while building a login test?
changes.newQuestion: Why is incognito mode particularly useful while building a login test?
oldKey: It guarantees a clean browser with no cookies or local storage, so the login flow is reliably exercised rather than skipped due to a remembered session.
newKey: A new incognito session reduces inherited browser cookies/storage, helping establish login preconditions.
changes.oldRationale: Running in incognito mode starts with a clean browser every time — no cookies, no local storage — so the test doesn't accidentally skip the login flow because the browser 'remembers' a prior session.
changes.newRationale: A fresh browser context helps avoid inherited browser authentication. It does not reset server-side account state or guarantee every SSO condition.

changes.oldQuestion: A login test sometimes fails because a previous run's session is still active and no login button appears. What is the recommended fix?
changes.newQuestion: A downstream flow permits an existing authenticated session and otherwise needs login. Which approach handles both starts?
oldKey: Add a condition that checks at runtime whether login is actually needed (e.g. is the login button visible), so the test handles both starting states.
newKey: Condition the login group on whether login is needed and assert the resulting authenticated state.
changes.oldRationale: Adding a condition that determines at runtime whether the login step should execute — such as checking if the login button is visible — lets the test work whether the session starts logged in or logged out.
changes.newRationale: Conditional login handles this downstream flow; verify the resulting state. A login-specific test should instead establish logged-out preconditions.

changes.oldQuestion: A team needs their mobile tests to run on their own local devices and be compatible with an existing Appium-based grid. Which recording mode should they use?
changes.newQuestion: A team needs their mobile tests to run on their own local devices and be compatible with an existing Appium-based grid. Which recording mode should they use?
oldKey: Appium mode, since it guarantees Appium-grid compatibility and supports local execution.
newKey: Standard Appium compatibility mode, with the required driver/device/grid setup.
changes.oldRationale: Appium mode guarantees compatibility with other Appium-based grids and supports local executions on local devices — exactly what this team needs, at the cost of being limited to Appium's own capabilities.
changes.newRationale: Standard Appium compatibility permits these execution targets with suitable setup; Enhanced is limited to VMG virtual devices.

changes.oldQuestion: Why might Appium mode struggle to fully record a hybrid app's flow?
changes.newQuestion: What limitation does Testim document for its Standard Appium compatibility recording mode?
oldKey: Because Appium mode is restricted to Appium's own capabilities, which can have gaps around hybrid apps and webviews.
newKey: Some hybrid/webview flows may not be fully recordable; verify the required flow and mode.
changes.oldRationale: Appium mode is restricted to Appium's capabilities, meaning some flows may not be fully recordable, especially with hybrid apps or webviews — Enhanced mode's zero-knowledge, unified API is built to handle this case instead.
changes.newRationale: Testim warns of mode-specific recording gaps. Enhanced supports documented frameworks on VMG, but neither app type nor framework name proves a particular flow works.
